line: ...Morning already.
Chat, he's awake. Say hi to Leon, chat.
Who are you talking to?
My chat. Well. Imaginary chat. No signal up here. But they're with me in spirit.
Hi, chat.
See? He gets it. Chat loves you, little man.
You're so weird, Luke.
Weird gets you subscribers. Kaylie says that. Okay, she doesn't. But she would.
Morning, sleepyhead. You were talking in your sleep again.
What did I say?
Something about pancakes. With syrup. You were very serious about the syrup.
My stomach hurts just hearing the word.
Don't step on my lupines when you get up.
They're in a pot, Rose.
Then don't step on the pot.
When they bloom I'm planting them by the porch. So it's the first thing anyone sees when they come up the road.
If anyone comes up the road.
They will.
They will, Rose.
Breakfast! Come down while it's warm!
Warm. She means wet.
Last of the oats. I'm sorry it's so thin.
Kaylie does fasting streams. Twenty-four hours, no food. Chat goes crazy for it.
That's not the same thing.
Eat, all of you. I'll figure something out.
Mom, you don't have any.
I ate already, honey.
Her bowl is clean. It's been clean for three days.
I could hike down. Find the highway. It's like, what, forty miles?
No. The pass is gone, Luke. You saw the road. You'd fall, and I'd never find you.
...Okay. Okay, Mom.
We could eat my flowers.
We are not eating your flowers.
Nasturtiums are edible! I read it!
Nobody is eating Rose's flowers.
Chores. Leon, water the garden and pull the weeds. Luke, firewood. Girls, laundry.
And the coop?
...Check it anyway. Maybe Biscuit's ghost left us an egg.
Not funny.
Little funny.
Forty swings per log. I counted. Content.
Nobody is watching, Luke.
Chat is always watching, Leon.
Real talk? I'm starving. Like, my hands shake. Don't tell Mom.
She's got enough going on.
Go water your carrots, farmer boy.
We're washing the same four shirts. Again.
They smell like woodsmoke forever now.
I like woodsmoke.
Go on, the garden needs you more than we do.
Still cold. At least the well never runs out.
They look a little less dead now.
Empty. Just feathers and old straw.
Biscuit was the last one. Rose made her a grave with a little cross.
Yo. It's almost noon. Signal Rock. You coming?
Mom said to stay close...
It's ten minutes up the hill. I'm a responsible adult. Come on.
Yeah!
Come on, come on, come on...
ONE BAR! Chat, we have ONE BAR!
Okay okay okay. Kaylie posted. She's streaming tonight. Eight o'clock.
And, dude. DUDE. She replied to my donation. From before the storm.
'Thanks Luke_Plays, you're the best.' She knows my name, Leon.
She says that to everyone.
Nah. She said my name. Like, the actual letters. That's different.
...You don't get it. It's fine.
That's awesome, Luke.
Right?! I told you. We're basically friends.
When the road opens I'm driving to her meetup in Denver. I'll be the guy who came down off a mountain. She'll remember that.
Aaand the bar is gone.
Hey. You see the road? Way down there, where it just... stops?
Yeah.
If it gets bad. Like, really bad. I'll hike out. Even if Mom says no. I'd do it for you guys.
Promise?
Promise. Now race you back. Loser does dishes.
I'm drawing the mountains. When I'm scared, I draw whatever's in front of me.
It makes the world hold still for a minute.
Go help Rose. She has been talking to those seedlings all day.
Finally. Okay. These are lupine seedlings. They're tougher than they look.
Fireweed is the first thing that grows after a forest burns. Did you know that? Everything burns down and then, pink. Everywhere.
Dig two holes. Not too deep. They have to be able to breathe.
See? Things grow. Even now.
Thanks, Leon. You're the only one who doesn't think it's stupid.
Hi, sweetie. Potato peel soup. Don't make that face.
Is there really nothing else?
A cup of flour. Some salt. Rose's tomatoes, when they're ripe.
I'm going to fix this, Leon. I promise you. I will not watch my babies starve.
She's been humming that song a lot. The one from the music box Dad left her.
Chat, rate this soup.
Zero out of ten.
Negative ten.
You're all terrible.
That's the first time she's laughed in weeks.
Mom, eat yours. Please.
I'm not very hungry, honey.
You always say that.
You know I love you all more than anything. Right? Whatever happens.
...Mom, that is super ominous.
Go wash up. Bed.
Night, chat.
Night, Luke's chat.
Night, lupines.
Night, everyone.
Night, Biscuit.
...Night, Biscuit.
Leon. Look out the window. See the W? That's Cassiopeia.
W.
...Go to sleep, Luke.
Sleep tight, my loves.
She stood there for a long time. Just... watching us.
I'm so thirsty. And I can hear something downstairs.
...Can't sleep, sweetie?
I was thirsty. What are you doing?
Sharpening your grandpa's hunting knife. I'm going hunting tomorrow. There are still deer up past the ridge.
You don't know how to hunt.
I'll learn. Go back to bed, Leon.
Chat, today's the day. Mom's going hunting and I'm her backup.
Since when do you hunt?
I've watched like forty survival streams. It's basically the same thing.
Mm. Is there breakfast?
...Probably not, Rose.
Luke? Can you come down, honey? I need your strong arms.
Strong arms. You hear that, chat?
No breakfast today, kids. I'm sorry.
I saved some crackers. Four. One each.
Luke, before I go up the ridge I need your help with the old chest freezer downstairs. If I bring something back, we need it cold.
Sure. Generator still have gas?
Enough.
Hold my phone, little man. If Kaylie DMs me, tell her I'm busy saving my family.
It's still warm from his hand.
Brb, chat.
The generator. They got it running.
...The generator stopped.
There. It started again. Probably just the freezer lid.
Hold still. I'm drawing you.
Why?
Because you're here. That's reason enough.
Do you remember Dad?
Just a beard. And the music box.
He left when you were two. Mom did everything after that. Every single thing.
That's why she's like this. She's not sleeping, Leon. I hear her walking around at night.
Is Mom okay?
I don't know. I think she's more scared than we are.
I saw her sharpening a knife last night. At three in the morning.
...She said she was going hunting.
Mom has never even gone fishing.
Whatever happens, we stick together. You, me, Rose, Luke. Okay?
Okay.
Here. Done. You look like a sad little bird.
Where's Luke?
Luke is finishing something down there.
I got us something special for dinner tonight.
You went hunting? You got a deer?
A big one. Luke's helping me break it down. It's a lot of work, sweetie.
Meat. Real meat. My mouth is watering so much it hurts.
...I didn't hear a gunshot. Did she even take the rifle?
...Oh my god.
It's sweet. Kind of like pork? I don't care. I don't care at all.
Should we save some for Luke?
Luke already ate, honey.
Mom, this is amazing.
Eat up. There's plenty more.
Luke's phone. In my pocket.
Luke's going to miss Kaylie's stream.
He'll catch the next one.
Luke's bed is empty.
He's still down there?
Mom said he's sleeping on the couch so he can keep an eye on the generator.
Luke hates the couch.
...Yeah.
He'll want it when he comes up.
Leon. You hear that?
Mom's cutting up the deer.
At two in the morning?
Thunk. Thunk. Thunk. I counted forty-one before I fell asleep.
He didn't come up. His bed's still made.
Luke has never made his bed in his entire life.
Let's not panic. We'll ask Mom. Okay?
Mom, where's Luke?
Luke left before dawn. He hiked out to get help. He's a grown man, Rose.
In the RAIN? Without his phone? His coat's still on the hook!
He took your father's old coat.
Dad's coat has been in a box in the attic for eleven years.
...Okay. Thank you, Mom.
Meat for breakfast. I never thought I would get sick of hunger.
I'm not hungry.
Eat, Rose. You're skin and bones.
Leon, the roof is leaking upstairs. Put a bucket under it. Then you can do what you like until the rain stops.
Plink. Plink. At least it sounds like something.
Hey. Come sit. I want to show you something.
Don't tell Rose. She'll panic.
That one is from summer. Before the storm.
I drew that last night. She stands at the basement door every night. Just stands there. In the dark.
I think Luke's still down there, Leon.
Why would Mom lie?
I don't know. That's what scares me.
Maybe he really did leave.
Without saying goodbye to you? Luke?
Breathe with me. In for four. Hold. Out for four.
There. We're okay. We're okay.
Hey, Leon. Made you some hot cocoa.
Last packet in the cupboard. Don't tell Rose.
Thanks, Lily. It's really warm.
Your garden's looking good. Better than anything I could grow.
Leon... do you know where Mom got that meat?
No. Also, where did Luke g-
LILY! WE NEED YOU IN THE BASEMENT! COME HELP!
COMING!
See you, Leon...
...Where did Luke go?
Lily's not here...
Go wash up for dinner, sweetie.
Her voice came from right behind the door.
Mom, where's Lily?
Lily's helping your brother with something. They'll be up later.
You said Luke left to get help.
...Did I?
Sit down, sweetie. Dinner is ready.
It's even better than last night...
I hate that it's better.
It's so quiet without them.
They're closer than you think, honey.
Eat, Rose.
Good girl. There's plenty more.
Two empty beds now. Lily's sketchbook is still on her pillow.
Leon? Can I sit with you?
I keep thinking about Lily's face when Mom yelled. She looked scared.
Here. It's a forget-me-not. I pressed it last summer.
So you don't forget me. Or them.
I'm not going to forget you, Rose. You're right here.
Tomorrow I'm going to ask Mom to let me see them. I just want to see them.
I'll come with you.
No. Someone has to finish the garden. You're the garden guy.
Don't go down there.
It's just the basement, Leon. It's our house.
Mom's humming in the hallway. The music box song. Over and over.
Morning. I'm making crowns. One for Lily, one for Luke, one for me.
And one for you, if you help me pick flowers in the meadow.
...Is that the radio? In the study?
Friday. That's tomorrow. They're coming TOMORROW.
Mom! The radio! They're coming! Road crews, on Friday! Tomorrow!
...That's wonderful, sweetie.
Tomorrow?! Luke can come back! Lily too! We can all go!
Yes. We can all go.
She didn't even blink.
Come on! Flowers! I want the crowns done before they get back!
Okay! I need three fireweed. The tall pink ones.
Two lupines. Blue-purple, like little towers. And one forget-me-not. Tiny and blue. That one is the hardest.
YOU FOUND ONE! Leon, you have the best eyes in this family.
Perfect. Sit. This takes a minute.
When the road opens, I'm going to plant a whole hill of lupines. Purple everywhere. You'll be able to see it from space.
And I'm going to study plants. Botany. Lily says I'd be good at it.
You'd be the best at it.
Here. Yours.
Fireweed is for starting over. Forget-me-nots are for... you know.
Mom, can I see what Luke and Lily are doing?
Sure, hun. Come down to the basement.
Hold Lily's crown for me. I'll bring her up to get it.
Rose too...?
They're so red this year.
Is that... ketchup?
Don't mind the mess, sweetie. Ketchup.
Sit down. Tonight is extra special.
Better than ever. So tender it falls apart.
Mom isn't eating. She's just... watching me.
Mom, where are Lily, Luke and Rose? Can I go see them?
...Of course you can, sweetie.
They're all downstairs. Come on.
They're right through here, sweetie. All together.
Luke...?
Lily...?
ROSE?!
wait...
is this where dinner came from..
i ate them?
Shh. Shh. It's okay, baby. You'll be with them now.
Kaylie. Luke's 'friend'. She has two million followers.
He has us.
Lily draws everything. The mountain, the chickens, us. She even drew Biscuit's grave.
I've read all of them nine times. I could recite Captain Comet #14 from memory.
"Sent to all subscribers." Luke would have died for that message.
...I shouldn't have read that.
Every day crossed off in red. "Road out?" with a question mark. Mom wrote that on day one.
Last summer. Luke's making a face. Lily's laughing. Rose is holding a flower. Mom looks so... young.
Static. Just static. Mom keeps it on low anyway. I think the noise helps her.
Padlocked. From this side.
The generator's so loud down there.
Locked.
Jars. Rows of them. Red, packed tight, sealed. Mom must have been up all night canning.
...We don't have any deer jars. We've never had a deer.
BISCUIT. GOOD GIRL. 2 EGGS A DAY. Rose painted it. There are fresh flowers on it.
Dad's old truck. No gas since the second week. Luke still sits in it sometimes to charge his phone with the crank.
Rose named him Gerald. Gerald isn't scaring anything. There's nothing left to scare.
KESSLER. Empty. Obviously. Nobody has been up the road in six weeks.
The road just... ends. A cliff where the pavement used to be. Mom says the creek took the whole hillside.
Old sweaters. A watch. And...
Dad's coat. Folded. Right here.
Mom said Luke took it.
